summary:
ITMF has named HeiQ and Archroma and Lenzing and Armedangels as winners of its 2026 International Collaboration Awards, recognising textile partnerships aligned with the UN Sustainable Development Goals.
The winners will present projects on scaling innovation and sustainable collaboration at the ITMF and IAF Conference in Fortaleza, Brazil, October 14–15.

title: ICE cotton plunges as weak demand, harvest pressure weigh
summary:
ICE December 2026 cotton settled at 82.17 cents per pound, down 2.60 per cent, losing 605 points over five sessions.
US Upland sales fell 30 per cent below the four-week average, while shipments were 26 per cent lower amid weak export demand.
Harvest pressure, a stronger dollar, softer crude oil and high open interest kept futures under pressure as traders assessed US crop yields.

title: Australian wool prices decline amid cautious buying ahead of Nanjing
summary:
Australia's wool market softened as a larger 28,392-bale offering met more selective buying, with the EMI down 21 cents to 1,857 Au$/kg.
Exporters and mills saw Chinese caution offset partly by European and Indian inventory replacement demand.
Supply remains tight, with season-to-date offerings 8.6 per cent lower, keeping EMI 38.2 per cent above a year ago.

title: Germany's manufacturing order stock rises 1.5% in July
summary:
Germany’s manufacturing order backlog rose 1.5 per cent in July 2026, reaching a record high and increasing 10.9 per cent year on year. 
Growth was driven mainly by other transport equipment. 
Domestic backlog growth outpaced foreign orders, while order coverage reached a record nine months.
Machinery backlogs increase, with capital goods recording the longest production coverage.

title: Bank of England holds Bank Rate at 3.75% amid inflation risks
summary:
BoE held the Bank Rate at 3.75 per cent in September, with a 6–3 MPC vote, as higher energy prices lifted UK inflation risks.
CPI rose to 3.1 per cent in August and may rise further, keeping cost, wage and demand pressures in focus for UK apparel retail and sourcing.
The MPC said it was ready to act to return inflation to 2 per cent, while annual £20 billion gilt sales will run to 2034.

title: LVMH’s luxury crown slips as consumer spending starts to shift
summary:
Bain-Altagamma says personal luxury goods fell 2 per cent to €358 billion ($410 billion) in 2025, before a 2026 rebound.
LVMH's H1 2026 revenue reached €38.6 billion ($44.28 billion), with Q2 organic growth at 3 per cent.
Europe tourist spending fell around 20 per cent in February 2026, Middle East mall traffic weakened, and L'Oréal briefly overtook LVMH.

title: Vietnam projected to lead SEA-6 growth at 6.2% annually through 2035
summary:
Vietnam is projected to record the fastest economic growth among Southeast Asia’s six largest economies, with average annual GDP growth of 6.2 per cent through 2035, according to a report by Bain & Company, DBS Bank and Vriens & Partners. 
The outlook is supported by manufacturing exports, foreign investment and Vietnam’s role in regional supply chains.

title: Fashion’s agentic AI race: What’s blocking the move beyond pilots?
summary:
AI agents are entering apparel product development, costing and sourcing through launches from PTC, Aptean and Centric.
Research warns up to 90 per cent of AI initiatives fail to scale beyond pilots, blocked by governance, data quality and fragmented tools.
Despite 92 per cent planning more AI investment, only 1 per cent report mature deployment; brands must fix product data.

title: Vietnam's outbound investment jumps 4.7-fold in January-August
summary:
Vietnam’s outbound investment rose 4.7-fold in the first eight months of 2026, while registered FDI reached $40.63 billion, up 55.4 per cent year on year. 
Trade turnover rose 28.7 per cent to $770.14 billion, and manufacturing PMI hit 53.3 in August, signalling continued expansion in production, trade and investment activity.
Business formation also strengthened during the period.

title: European hourly labour costs rise 3.1% in euro area, 3.2% in EU
summary:
European hourly labour costs rose 3.1 per cent year on year in the euro area and 3.2 per cent in the EU in Q2 2026, according to the Eurostat.
Construction recorded the strongest increase among business activities at 3.9 per cent in both regions. 
Bulgaria, Lithuania and Croatia posted the highest wage-cost growth, while Luxembourg and Romania recorded the lowest.

title: Bangladesh's garment exports to EU fall 13.65% in January-July 2026
summary:
Bangladesh’s garment exports to the European Union fell 13.65 per cent year on year to €10.37 billion in January-July 2026, significantly exceeding the EU’s overall 5.10 per cent decline in garment imports. 
China and Vietnam recorded export growth during the period, while Bangladesh also saw lower shipment volumes and average export prices.

title: India apparel exports slide 11% as $6.5 bn sourcing prize emerges
summary:
India’s apparel retail market is estimated at ₹9.3 lakh crore in FY25 and projected at ₹16 lakh crore by FY30, with organised retail at about 41 per cent.
TexPro shows 2025 exports still below 2015 levels; H1 2026 exports fell 11.2 per cent, while imports rose 13.3 per cent.
Nearly 2,000 planned fashion-store openings could create about $6.5 billion in additional garment and allied sourcing.

title: New ₹2,000 UPI rule tests ₹27,000-cr apparel payment market
summary:
From October 15, qualifying UPI purchases above ₹2,000 incur a 0.4 per cent merchant fee; customers pay no surcharge.
Apparel is close to the cut-off: August 2026 average UPI tickets were ₹886 at family-clothing shops and ₹1,195 at men's and women's stores.
India's apparel exports fell 11.2 per cent in H1 2026; festive period contributes nearly 35 per cent of annual apparel sales.

title: South Korean apparel imports rise 2.8% in January-August 2026
summary:

Knitted apparel imports grew 4.64 per cent and non-knitted apparel imports rose 1.47 per cent in the first eight months.
Exports of man-made filaments fell 4.32 per cent, while knitted or crocheted fabrics gained 8.56 per cent.

title: Is mono-fabric design changing the future of waterproof outerwear?
summary:
BAM launched the Any Weather Mac in September 2026, describing it as the UK’s first certified-recyclable waterproof coat.
The coat uses mono-fabric construction, about 90-95 per cent recycled polyester, a virgin CoPES membrane and a removable zinc-alloy zip head.
It has a PFAS-free finish, 10,000mm rating, welded seams, take-back route and Infinitee certification.

title: US’ Gap Inc appoints Kirsten Green to board of directors
summary:
Gap Inc has appointed Forerunner founder and managing partner Kirsten Green to its board of directors with immediate effect.
Green brings venture investment experience in consumer-led growth, scaling brands and anticipating shifts in customer behaviour.
The move supports Gap Inc’s transformation as it strengthens core apparel businesses and expands brand reach into beauty and accessories.

title: BKMEA urges Bangladesh govt to form garment policy panel
summary:
BKMEA has urged Bangladesh's government to create a high-level committee to coordinate garment-sector policymaking. 
The proposed body would bring ministries, revenue officials and apparel-textile associations together to address industry issues. 
The agenda covers fair codes, energy planning, stakeholder-led policy changes, transport digitalisation and building-code implementation.

title: Global apparel trade 2026: Who wins the $550 bn share war?
summary:
China, Bangladesh and Vietnam dominate the $546.8 billion garment market, with 2026 sourcing flows splintering across more countries.
US apparel imports fell 8.65 per cent in January-July 2026; Vietnam led; Bangladesh stayed ahead of China and Cambodia rose 10.48 per cent.
Buyers are using more sourcing markets but consolidating around suppliers with flexibility, traceability and compliance.

title: Can Indian apparel exporters beat the rising cost crunch?
summary:
Cotton yarn prices in India have risen from about ₹250 a kg in early 2026 to around ₹400, pressuring apparel exporters’ fabric and garment costs.
AEPC has urged government action to regulate cotton-yarn exports of 20s count and above as flows to Bangladesh and Vietnam increase.
Tiruppur estimates production costs are up 15 per cent; raw cotton duty relief may be extended beyond October 31.

title: India's apparel retail revenue to grow 12-13% in FY27: Crisil Ratings
summary:
Crisil Ratings projects 12-13 per cent revenue growth for organised apparel retail in India this fiscal, down from about 15 per cent last year.
Value fashion and tier-II, tier-III expansion are driving volumes, but rising cotton and operating costs may pull margins to 14 per cent.
Festive demand, store productivity and responsive sourcing will shape full-year performance and supplier planning.
